Let \(b_n=\frac1{a_n}\). Since \(S_n\) is the sum of the arithmetic sequence \(\{b_n\}\),

\[
\frac{S_n}{n}=\frac{b_1+b_n}{2}=b_1+\frac{(n-1)d}{2}.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{S_5}{5}+\frac{S_{11}}{11}
=(b_1+2d)+(b_1+5d)=2b_1+7d=12.
\]

Now

\[
S_8=8\cdot \frac{S_8}{8}
=8\left(b_1+\frac{7d}{2}\right)
=4(2b_1+7d)
=4\cdot 12
=48.
\]

\[
\boxed{48}
\]
